## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

The retry helper must enforce the project’s five-attempt cap before merge because a persistent upstream failure currently triggers ten calls by default.

## Changes

The pull request adds `fetch_with_retry` with configurable attempts and delay, adds retry tests and a review fixture, and proposes raising the documented attempt cap from five to ten.

## Critical

- app/net.py:13 — correctness — Cap retries at five attempts — A default call makes ten fetches when the upstream keeps raising `OSError`, and the validation also accepts an explicit ten. `AGENTS.md:5` says “Retry helpers under app/ must cap attempts at 5.” — During a sustained outage, each default call can send five extra requests before returning the failure. — Fix: Set both the default and validation ceiling to five, and update `test_fetch_with_retry_default_attempt_count` and `test_fetch_with_retry_rejects_attempts_outside_range`.

## Important

(none)

## Suggestions

- app/net.py:14 — comments — Document which exceptions trigger retries — A response that ends before its declared `Content-Length` fails on the first attempt with `IncompleteRead`. The docstring says “Call fetch until it succeeds or attempts calls have failed,” but the loop catches only `except OSError:`. — Callers who rely on the documented behavior can receive an immediate error when an upstream sends a truncated response.
